policy_title: Invest in High-Quality Early Years Education
stated: Invest in high-quality early years education and close the attainment gap by giving disadvantaged children aged three and four an extra five free hours a week and tripling the Early Years Pupil Premium to £1,000 a year.

source.quote: Invest in high-quality early years education and close the attainment gap by giving disadvantaged children aged three and four an extra five free hours a week and tripling the Early Years Pupil Premium to £1,000 a year.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly targets early years education quality and the attainment gap for disadvantaged 3–4 year-olds via extra funded hours and a tripled Early Years Pupil Premium — core indicators of this fundamental.

An extra five free hours of childcare per week materially reduces out-of-pocket childcare costs for disadvantaged families, who face some of the highest proportional childcare burdens, earning a real verdict on household affordability.

By redistributing educational resource specifically to disadvantaged children, the policy bears on the intergenerational dimension of the rich-poor gap: early childhood investment is among the most evidence-backed mechanisms for narrowing lifetime earnings inequality (Heckman curve), so the gap between top and bottom is a genuine indicator this policy moves.

membership_note: Two fundamentals: O7 is the designed-for outcome; O14 earns a genuine cross-outcome verdict because the policy is explicitly redistributive (targeted at disadvantaged children) with a nameable mechanism linking early-years quality to lifetime inequality. Fiscal cost is real but the policy presents this as a funded investment and the spend is unlikely to alone materially shift the debt-sustainability path, so O12 is omitted at this stage.
